chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about a man who made a bequest at the time of his death that Hajj be performed on his behalf. He said: 'If he had already performed Hajj, then it should be taken from one-third of his estate; and if he had not performed Hajj, then from the main body of his wealth, and no other [source] is permissible.'

key_terms.ثُلُثِهِ: One-third of his estate (the portion for bequests)
key_terms.صُلْبِ مَالِهِ: The main body of his wealth (the remaining two-thirds for heirs)

ai.seo_question: What is the source of funds for Hajj if a deceased person bequeathed it but had not yet performed the obligatory pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the distinction between fulfilling a specific bequest (wasiyyah) versus discharging a personal obligation (fard) after death. If the Hajj was already obligatory and performed, the expense is treated as a debt against the one-third bequest portion; if not yet performed, it is paid from the principal estate (the two-thirds for heirs) to ensure the religious duty is completed. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligatory Hajj takes precedence over the distribution of the remaining inheritance.
